description: Enforce automatic zero-initialization of kernel stack variables and heap allocations via CONFIG_INIT_STACK_ALL_ZERO and CONFIG_INIT_ON_ALLOC_DEFAULT_ON. These kernel build options ensure that uninitialized memory contains zeros rather than stale data, preventing information disclosure from uninitialized reads and blocking exploitation of uninitialized pointer dereferences. CONFIG_INIT_ON_FREE_DEFAULT_ON zeros memory on deallocation, further reducing the window for use-after-free exploitation by ensuring freed memory does not contain exploitable pointers or data. The runtime equivalent init_on_alloc=1 and init_on_free=1 kernel boot parameters provide the same behavior without requiring a kernel rebuild. Performance overhead is typically 1-3% for init_on_alloc and 1-5% for init_on_free depending on allocation-heavy workloads.

conditions: Requires kernel compiled with CONFIG_INIT_STACK_ALL_ZERO and CONFIG_INIT_ON_ALLOC_DEFAULT_ON, or booted with init_on_alloc=1 init_on_free=1 parameters.

cvss_vector_impacts.rationale: Exploit must work with zero-initialized memory rather than attacker-favorable stale values; finding useful uninitialized data paths becomes significantly harder because stack variables, heap allocations, and freed memory all contain zeros instead of exploitable pointers or data
Information disclosure via uninitialized memory reads returns zeros instead of kernel pointers, stack data, or heap contents that would enable KASLR bypass or credential theft

relationships.rationale: Zero-initialization ensures uninitialized pointers are NULL rather than containing exploitable stale addresses
Directly eliminates use of uninitialized resources by ensuring all memory starts at zero
Prevents use of uninitialized variables by enforcing zero-initialization at allocation
Eliminates information leaks through uninitialized memory reads by ensuring no stale data persists
Enforces proper initialization at the kernel allocator level regardless of application code

verification.method: Verify kernel is built with memory initialization options or booted with init_on_alloc/init_on_free parameters
